transcript.text: Hi everyone. As you know, I've been holding onto Grandma's coin collection — all 42 coins — since she passed. With my move to a smaller apartment coming up, we need to settle what happens to the collection. Before we start discussing options, I want to do my usual check-in: Jordan, Rosa, do either of you know of any promises or care requirements concerning particular coins or groups in the collection?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have something relevant. Last month I got a written assessment from our family appraiser, Helen Park. She said the three 1909 Lincoln cents must remain together as a group and should be stored in acid-free capsules for preservation. I hadn't had a chance to share this with everyone yet, but it seems important for the settlement.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have something too. I have a dated birthday card from Grandma where she promised me the 1921 Morgan silver dollar from the collection. I haven't had a chance to show it to either of you yet, but I've kept it all this time.
transcript.speaker: A3
